text:
**Short version:** Qi2 and Qi2.2 are open standards from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). MagSafe is Apple's branded version, and it now overlaps with both.

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who | WPC standard | WPC standard | Apple's brand and certification program |
| Max speed | 15W | 25W | 15W on most iPhones, up to 25W on newer ones |
| Magnets | Yes | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2** added a magnetic ring to Qi so the phone and charger align, which improves efficiency and speed. Apple contributed its MagSafe tech to it ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)). It's capped at 15W ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** is the 25W update, with nearly 70% more power. The WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes. Certified products began appearing in July 2025 ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/), [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's own term. Apple-certified MagSafe accessories deliver 15W to most iPhones and up to 25W to the iPhone 16 and 17 series. Certified ones also have an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, plus a magnetometer to prevent compass interference ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Apple's current MagSafe Charger is also certified for Qi2 25W ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8)).

**Things to watch for:**
- **"MagSafe-compatible" isn't the same as MagSafe-certified.** These chargers usually just add magnets and often run at 7.5W ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Look for the Qi2 or Qi2 25W logo, and you can check the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).
- **Your phone sets the speed.** For full 25W you need an iPhone 16 or 17 series with a 30W+ adapter. Apple lists the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro at 22.5W peak and the iPhone Air at 20W. The iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier top out at 15W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)). The iPhone 16e has no magnetic charging.
- **Android support is thin.** The Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W. Other Pixel 10 models do 15W, and Samsung's Galaxy S26 is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**If you want a 25W charger:**
- [Apple MagSafe Charger (1 m or 2 m)](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8). The 2 m is $49 on Apple's page, and Macworld listed the 1 m at $39. It's certified for both MagSafe and Qi2 25W.
- [Baseus PicoGo AM52 Qi2.2 power bank](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w), a 10,000 mAh battery for on the go. The Verge found it had the fastest wireless charging of the seven it tested ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)). It's $59.99 at Baseus, or $53.99 with code AM52 (last tested Oct 24, 2026). That's an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy.
